assessments.title: Entrepreneurship: Customer discovery and evidence — Imara Tutorial 01-001
assessments.description: Apply customer discovery and evidence to an illustrative venture considering a reusable-packaging route for small workshop owners. Reason from the stated evidence, separate facts from assumptions, and account for this scenario's constraint: unneeded customer records should not be collected.
learning_objectives: Distinguish observed behavior from assumptions and interpretations.
Design non-leading questions about recent customer experiences.
Use evidence limits and informed consent to choose a discovery step.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Imara Tutorial 01-001 is considering a reusable-packaging route for small workshop owners. Its current evidence is that observations found repeat manual entry at one handoff; one constraint is that unneeded customer records should not be collected. What is the strongest next discovery step?
options: Ask friends to estimate the size of the market.
Build the complete product before another conversation.
Ask target customers to describe a recent occasion when the difficulty occurred and what they did.
Pitch the proposed solution and ask whether they like it.
questions.correct_answer: Ask target customers to describe a recent occasion when the difficulty occurred and what they did.
questions.rationale: A recent account of actual behavior is stronger evidence than praise, forecasts, or a reaction to a pitch.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Imara Tutorial 01-001 is considering a reusable-packaging route for small workshop owners. Its current evidence is that observations found repeat manual entry at one handoff; one constraint is that unneeded customer records should not be collected. Which conclusion stays within the stated evidence?
options: The planned feature will solve the problem for everyone.
Report only the specific observation described, without extending it to the whole market.
Every potential customer would pay for the offer.
The difficulty is the market's most urgent problem.
questions.correct_answer: Report only the specific observation described, without extending it to the whole market.
questions.rationale: A defensible fact stays within the evidence's scope; general demand and future outcomes remain hypotheses.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Imara Tutorial 01-001 is considering a reusable-packaging route for small workshop owners. Its current evidence is that observations found repeat manual entry at one handoff; one constraint is that unneeded customer records should not be collected. Which interview prompt is least leading?
options: Tell me about the last time you handled this task.
Would an app make this easier for you?
You would pay to avoid this, right?
Which of our features do you like most?
questions.correct_answer: Tell me about the last time you handled this task.
questions.rationale: An open question about a specific past event does not embed the founder's preferred answer.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Imara Tutorial 01-001 is considering a reusable-packaging route for small workshop owners. Its current evidence is that observations found repeat manual entry at one handoff; one constraint is that unneeded customer records should not be collected. What best indicates meaningful problem severity?
options: A respondent says the idea sounds interesting.
A social post receives positive reactions.
A friend encourages the founder.
Repeated workarounds with a described cost in time, money, or effort.
questions.correct_answer: Repeated workarounds with a described cost in time, money, or effort.
questions.rationale: Behavior and consequences offer stronger evidence of severity than compliments.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Imara Tutorial 01-001 is considering a reusable-packaging route for small workshop owners. Its current evidence is that observations found repeat manual entry at one handoff; one constraint is that unneeded customer records should not be collected. How can a founder reduce interview sampling bias?
options: Ask only users of one competing product.
Use the founder's own experience as the full sample.
Include people with recent experience who use different workarounds.
Interview only enthusiastic followers.
questions.correct_answer: Include people with recent experience who use different workarounds.
questions.rationale: Relevant variation exposes alternatives and reduces reliance on friendly or unusually engaged respondents.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Imara Tutorial 01-001 is considering a reusable-packaging route for small workshop owners. Its current evidence is that observations found repeat manual entry at one handoff; one constraint is that unneeded customer records should not be collected. What belongs in a useful interview record?
options: A polished theory that replaces the customer's account.
Context, reported actions, and a separately labeled interpretation.
A summary containing only evidence that supports the idea.
A future purchase prediction recorded as fact.
questions.correct_answer: Context, reported actions, and a separately labeled interpretation.
questions.rationale: Separating observation from interpretation makes later review more reliable.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Imara Tutorial 01-001 is considering a reusable-packaging route for small workshop owners. Its current evidence is that observations found repeat manual entry at one handoff; one constraint is that unneeded customer records should not be collected. Similar difficulty, different workarounds: what next?
options: Compare contexts and desired outcomes before grouping the accounts.
Treat all respondents as identical because the task has the same name.
Discard all but the most dramatic account.
Immediately build a separate product for everyone.
questions.correct_answer: Compare contexts and desired outcomes before grouping the accounts.
questions.rationale: Similar symptoms can arise in different contexts, so compare needs before defining a segment.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Imara Tutorial 01-001 is considering a reusable-packaging route for small workshop owners. Its current evidence is that observations found repeat manual entry at one handoff; one constraint is that unneeded customer records should not be collected. Before recording an interview, what is appropriate?
options: Record quietly to keep the conversation natural.
Promise no one could ever access the recording.
Collect unrelated personal details for possible later use.
Explain the purpose, obtain permission, and offer participation without recording.
questions.correct_answer: Explain the purpose, obtain permission, and offer participation without recording.
questions.rationale: Informed permission and data minimization respect participants without making unsupported security promises.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Imara Tutorial 01-001 is considering a reusable-packaging route for small workshop owners. Its current evidence is that observations found repeat manual entry at one handoff; one constraint is that unneeded customer records should not be collected. What is a useful decision rule after discovery interviews?
options: Continue until someone agrees with the founder.
Choose a success threshold after seeing the results.
State what evidence would strengthen or weaken the problem hypothesis.
Declare fit if one person requests a feature.
questions.correct_answer: State what evidence would strengthen or weaken the problem hypothesis.
questions.rationale: A prior rule limits confirmation bias and makes contrary evidence useful.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Imara Tutorial 01-001 is considering a reusable-packaging route for small workshop owners. Its current evidence is that observations found repeat manual entry at one handoff; one constraint is that unneeded customer records should not be collected. A workaround exists but urgency is unclear. What should be tested?
options: Treat stated buying intention as a completed purchase.
How often the situation occurs and what customers currently sacrifice to address it.
Assume the workaround is used frequently.
Add features to make the offer sound valuable.
questions.correct_answer: How often the situation occurs and what customers currently sacrifice to address it.
questions.rationale: Frequency and current sacrifice help assess importance before committing to a solution.

assessments.concept_explanation: Customer discovery investigates what people do, in which circumstances, and with what consequences; it is not a vote on a finished idea.
assessments.terminology_and_components: A hypothesis needs testing; an observation is recorded information; an interpretation explains it; a workaround is an existing response to a task.
assessments.why_it_matters: Separating evidence from belief helps limited resources go toward demonstrated needs rather than imagined demand.
assessments.how_it_works: Recruit people with relevant recent experience, ask open questions about specific events, capture context, and compare patterns and counterexamples.
assessments.worked_examples: For Imara Tutorial 01-001, ask a small workshop owners about the last occasion involving a reusable-packaging route; record the workaround and consequence, and label future purchase claims untested.
assessments.common_mistakes: Leading questions, friendly-only samples, and treating compliments as demand distort learning. A small interview set cannot establish market prevalence.
assessments.practical_application: Prepare a guide about recent events, request recording permission, and separate accounts from interpretation. Consider: observations found repeat manual entry at one handoff.
assessments.decisions_and_tradeoffs: A larger round can reveal variation but costs time; choose the next sample to resolve a decision and state uncertainty.
assessments.related_concepts: Discovery informs segmentation, problem framing, value propositions, and MVP experiments; each requires evidence appropriate to its claim.

A problem statement lists a symptom but no cause. Improve it how?
options: Repeat the symptom more confidently as a cause.
Assume the most visible competitor caused it.
Replace the problem with a preferred feature.
Investigate the conditions that produce the symptom before stating a cause.
questions.correct_answer: Investigate the conditions that produce the symptom before stating a cause.
questions.rationale: Separating observation from explanation prevents an untested cause from becoming a specification.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Fursa Tutorial 02-016 is considering a bicycle maintenance visit for community event organizers. Its current evidence is that a pilot logged requests separately from incomplete attempts; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. How should two candidate segments be compared?
options: Pick the easiest story for investors.
Build a generic offer without comparison.
Apply the same evidence, urgency, access, and service criteria to both.
Choose the segment with the largest unverified estimate.
questions.correct_answer: Apply the same evidence, urgency, access, and service criteria to both.
questions.rationale: Consistent criteria make trade-offs visible and tie the choice to evidence.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Fursa Tutorial 02-016 is considering a bicycle maintenance visit for community event organizers. Its current evidence is that a pilot logged requests separately from incomplete attempts; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. What is wrong with a problem frame that says 'people need an app'?
options: It identifies a testable consequence.
It prescribes a solution before establishing the underlying customer difficulty.
It names a customer and specific situation.
It separates evidence from interpretation.
questions.correct_answer: It prescribes a solution before establishing the underlying customer difficulty.
questions.rationale: Needing an app is a solution hypothesis; first investigate who struggles, when, and why.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Fursa Tutorial 02-016 is considering a bicycle maintenance visit for community event organizers. Its current evidence is that a pilot logged requests separately from incomplete attempts; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. Why include doing nothing among existing alternatives?
options: It shows the baseline customers accept and what a new offer must improve.
It proves a new venture cannot succeed.
It removes the need for customer conversations.
It guarantees copied features will attract users.
questions.correct_answer: It shows the baseline customers accept and what a new offer must improve.
questions.rationale: Inaction and workarounds are genuine comparison points and can reveal switching costs.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Fursa Tutorial 02-016 is considering a bicycle maintenance visit for community event organizers. Its current evidence is that a pilot logged requests separately from incomplete attempts; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. A promising segment is hard to reach. What is prudent?
options: Ignore access because need automatically creates customers.
Assume promotion will solve access at any cost.
Redefine the segment to inflate the plan.
Test a realistic access route before making a commitment to serve it.
questions.correct_answer: Test a realistic access route before making a commitment to serve it.
questions.rationale: Reachability is a hypothesis and a real constraint on acquiring and serving customers.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Fursa Tutorial 02-016 is considering a bicycle maintenance visit for community event organizers. Its current evidence is that a pilot logged requests separately from incomplete attempts; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. When should a broad group be split into segments?
options: Only when a competitor uses separate labels.
Never; every customer should receive the same offer.
When context, need, buying process, or service differences change the offer or economics.
Whenever two people use different words.
questions.correct_answer: When context, need, buying process, or service differences change the offer or economics.
questions.rationale: Segmentation matters when differences change product, channel, or delivery decisions.

assessments.concept_explanation: Problem framing identifies who seeks progress, in what situation, what difficulty occurs, and why it matters without prescribing a solution.
assessments.terminology_and_components: A segment shares relevant context or needs; a job is progress sought in a circumstance; a symptom is observed while a cause remains an explanation.
assessments.why_it_matters: A bounded frame guides discovery and product choices better than an unfocused audience or an untested feature request.
assessments.how_it_works: Describe customer and situation, state observed obstacle and consequence, then compare segments by evidence, urgency, access, and delivery needs.
assessments.worked_examples: For Fursa Tutorial 02-016, examine community event organizers circumstances around a bicycle maintenance visit; a pilot logged requests separately from incomplete attempts can be tested, while customers need clear terms before a deposit is an operating condition, not proof of need.
assessments.common_mistakes: Calling everyone a segment, treating a feature request as a job, or stating a symptom as a proven cause weakens the frame.
assessments.practical_application: Draft alternative problem statements, list confirming and disconfirming observations, and identify which differences change the offer.
assessments.decisions_and_tradeoffs: A narrow segment improves focus but may constrain access; a broad segment may hide meaningful differences. Pick a testable starting group.
assessments.related_concepts: Customer jobs connect discovery with value propositions; segmentation also informs MVP recruitment, channels, pricing, and operations.

assessments.title: Entrepreneurship: MVP design and experimentation — Pishi Tutorial 03-017
assessments.description: Apply mvp design and experimentation to an illustrative venture considering a produce-ordering service for students sharing equipment. Reason from the stated evidence, separate facts from assumptions, and account for this scenario's constraint: the team cannot control the delivery date.
learning_objectives: Select an MVP that tests a named risky assumption.
Choose behavioral measures and decision thresholds before testing.
Interpret pilot evidence with limitations and safeguards.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Pishi Tutorial 03-017 is considering a produce-ordering service for students sharing equipment. Its current evidence is that interviews described the same workaround but different triggers; one constraint is that the team cannot control the delivery date. What makes an MVP useful?
options: It includes every requested feature.
It is a polished launch that avoids uncertainty.
It is the smallest credible test of a risky customer or solution assumption.
It is any cheap incomplete version.
questions.correct_answer: It is the smallest credible test of a risky customer or solution assumption.
questions.rationale: An MVP is defined by learning purpose and risk reduction, not just cost or feature count.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Pishi Tutorial 03-017 is considering a produce-ordering service for students sharing equipment. Its current evidence is that interviews described the same workaround but different triggers; one constraint is that the team cannot control the delivery date. The team assumes customers will request a consultation. What test fits?
options: Count page views as completed requests.
Offer a clear manual booking route and observe qualified requests.
Build automated scheduling before measuring demand.
Ask people whether booking sounds convenient.
questions.correct_answer: Offer a clear manual booking route and observe qualified requests.
questions.rationale: A manual test can observe behavior before investment in automation.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Pishi Tutorial 03-017 is considering a produce-ordering service for students sharing equipment. Its current evidence is that interviews described the same workaround but different triggers; one constraint is that the team cannot control the delivery date. If the hypothesis concerns taking a next step, what should a landing-page test measure?
options: A defined action by the intended audience, such as a qualified request.
Impressions without audience or action context.
The number of design revisions.
Compliments from people who did not see the offer.
questions.correct_answer: A defined action by the intended audience, such as a qualified request.
questions.rationale: The measure should correspond to the hypothesized behavior and define a qualified response.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Pishi Tutorial 03-017 is considering a produce-ordering service for students sharing equipment. Its current evidence is that interviews described the same workaround but different triggers; one constraint is that the team cannot control the delivery date. Why test a prototype using a narrow task?
options: Prove the entire business model is profitable.
Avoid choosing appropriate users.
Guarantee production software will behave identically.
Observe whether intended users can complete that task and where friction occurs.
questions.correct_answer: Observe whether intended users can complete that task and where friction occurs.
questions.rationale: A prototype can test a defined interaction, not every product or business assumption.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Pishi Tutorial 03-017 is considering a produce-ordering service for students sharing equipment. Its current evidence is that interviews described the same workaround but different triggers; one constraint is that the team cannot control the delivery date. A pilot has few responses. What should be reported?
options: Only the most favorable anecdote.
A result excluding nonresponses without disclosure.
Invitations, eligibility, response process, observed result, and limitations.
A market-wide estimate from the pilot alone.
questions.correct_answer: Invitations, eligibility, response process, observed result, and limitations.
questions.rationale: Transparent denominators and limitations prevent overstatement.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Pishi Tutorial 03-017 is considering a produce-ordering service for students sharing equipment. Its current evidence is that interviews described the same workaround but different triggers; one constraint is that the team cannot control the delivery date. Why set a success threshold before an experiment?
options: It removes the need to define behavior.
It reduces reinterpretation of an ambiguous outcome after results are visible.
It guarantees support for the hypothesis.
It makes a small sample representative.
questions.correct_answer: It reduces reinterpretation of an ambiguous outcome after results are visible.
questions.rationale: A prior decision rule limits moving goalposts without predetermining results.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Pishi Tutorial 03-017 is considering a produce-ordering service for students sharing equipment. Its current evidence is that interviews described the same workaround but different triggers; one constraint is that the team cannot control the delivery date. When is a concierge MVP useful?
options: When manual delivery can test customer value before automation.
When manual labor hides a cost that makes delivery unworkable.
When claiming scalability without testing it.
When customer consent is unnecessary.
questions.correct_answer: When manual delivery can test customer value before automation.
questions.rationale: Manual service can isolate value early, but labor and the nature of the trial must be disclosed.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Pishi Tutorial 03-017 is considering a produce-ordering service for students sharing equipment. Its current evidence is that interviews described the same workaround but different triggers; one constraint is that the team cannot control the delivery date. To test whether a feature reduces errors, what design fits?
options: Ask users if they expect fewer errors.
Change the task midway through every session.
Measure sign-ups and infer error reduction.
Define the task and error first, then observe intended users doing that task.
questions.correct_answer: Define the task and error first, then observe intended users doing that task.
questions.rationale: The test should observe the named outcome under a consistent task definition.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Pishi Tutorial 03-017 is considering a produce-ordering service for students sharing equipment. Its current evidence is that interviews described the same workaround but different triggers; one constraint is that the team cannot control the delivery date. An MVP misses its threshold. What is a responsible response?
options: Change the threshold until the test passes.
Conclude every possible customer will respond the same way.
Check test validity, then revise or reject the assumption according to evidence.
Hide the result and keep building.
questions.correct_answer: Check test validity, then revise or reject the assumption according to evidence.
questions.rationale: A failed test weakens an assumption within its limits; it does not prove a universal conclusion.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Pishi Tutorial 03-017 is considering a produce-ordering service for students sharing equipment. Its current evidence is that interviews described the same workaround but different triggers; one constraint is that the team cannot control the delivery date. What should be excluded from an MVP unless it supports the test?
options: A clear explanation of what the pilot provides.
Polish or automation unrelated to learning or safe delivery.
Consent and safety information needed by participants.
The mechanism needed to observe behavior.
questions.correct_answer: Polish or automation unrelated to learning or safe delivery.
questions.rationale: Remove nonessential scope but retain honest disclosure and appropriate safeguards.

assessments.concept_explanation: An MVP is a limited test of a consequential assumption; it is not an excuse for unsafe delivery or hidden limitations.
assessments.terminology_and_components: A hypothesis names an uncertain claim; a measure defines an observable result; a threshold informs a decision; a prototype explores an interaction.
assessments.why_it_matters: Testing uncertainty before broad building can conserve resources while keeping customer promises within the team's capacity.
assessments.how_it_works: State assumption, participant, procedure, measure, and decision rule in advance; run the smallest credible test and document its limits.
assessments.worked_examples: For Pishi Tutorial 03-017, a manual a produce-ordering service trial could test one action before automation; define the action, disclose limits, and account for the team cannot control the delivery date.
assessments.common_mistakes: Page visits are not purchases; stated interest is not use. Changing audience, offer, and success threshold after results harms interpretation.
assessments.practical_application: Choose a risky claim from interviews described the same workaround but different triggers, define a behavioral measure, and record incomplete attempts. Avoid unnecessary personal data.
assessments.decisions_and_tradeoffs: Manual delivery speeds learning but can hide labor costs; match test fidelity to the decision and safeguard participants.
assessments.related_concepts: MVP design draws on discovery, problem framing, experiment design, operations, and unit economics; results can inform but not guarantee a pivot.

assessments.title: Entrepreneurship: Unit economics and cash reasoning — Tendaji Tutorial 04-025
assessments.description: Apply unit economics and cash reasoning to an illustrative venture considering a tailoring pickup service for small offices managing supplies. Reason from the stated evidence, separate facts from assumptions, and account for this scenario's constraint: customers need clear terms before a deposit.
learning_objectives: Separate variable costs, fixed costs, contribution, profit, and cash.
Apply break-even reasoning to stated assumptions.
Use scenarios to reveal sensitivity to uncertain economic inputs.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Tendaji Tutorial 04-025 is considering a tailoring pickup service for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a prototype exposed confusion at one step; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. How is contribution per sale calculated?
options: Fixed costs divided by competitors.
Cash balance plus unpaid invoices.
Revenue per sale minus variable costs attributable to that sale.
Revenue minus every historical startup expense.
questions.correct_answer: Revenue per sale minus variable costs attributable to that sale.
questions.rationale: Contribution is available toward fixed costs; it is not identical to profit or cash.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Tendaji Tutorial 04-025 is considering a tailoring pickup service for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a prototype exposed confusion at one step; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. Orders have positive contribution but overhead is uncovered. What follows?
options: An unpaid invoice counts as received cash.
More contribution volume, improved unit economics, or lower fixed costs may be needed for break-even.
The business is already profitable.
Overhead can be ignored.
questions.correct_answer: More contribution volume, improved unit economics, or lower fixed costs may be needed for break-even.
questions.rationale: Per-unit contribution alone does not establish that fixed obligations are covered.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Tendaji Tutorial 04-025 is considering a tailoring pickup service for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a prototype exposed confusion at one step; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. Which is a variable cost per delivery?
options: Packaging and courier charges incurred for each fulfilled order.
A monthly lease unchanged by order volume.
A registration fee already paid once.
A long-term strategic objective.
questions.correct_answer: Packaging and courier charges incurred for each fulfilled order.
questions.rationale: A variable cost changes with transactions or units; the other examples do not in this scenario.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Tendaji Tutorial 04-025 is considering a tailoring pickup service for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a prototype exposed confusion at one step; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. Why account for founder labor in unit economics?
options: It makes unpaid time current cash expenditure.
It eliminates fixed costs.
It turns labor into sales revenue.
It reveals dependence on unpaid work that may later need to be paid or replaced.
questions.correct_answer: It reveals dependence on unpaid work that may later need to be paid or replaced.
questions.rationale: Valuing owner labor exposes economic dependence without misclassifying current cash flow.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Tendaji Tutorial 04-025 is considering a tailoring pickup service for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a prototype exposed confusion at one step; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. Given fixed costs and positive unit contribution, how estimate break-even quantity?
options: Divide variable cost by fixed costs.
Multiply cash balance by price.
Divide fixed costs by contribution per unit using consistent assumptions.
Divide revenue by employee count.
questions.correct_answer: Divide fixed costs by contribution per unit using consistent assumptions.
questions.rationale: The ratio estimates units needed for contribution to cover fixed costs under the model.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Tendaji Tutorial 04-025 is considering a tailoring pickup service for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a prototype exposed confusion at one step; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. The delivery method changes. What should be recalculated?
options: Treat each extra delivery as pure margin.
Variable cost, capacity, and contribution under the new method.
Nothing because price stayed the same.
Only social reactions to the announcement.
questions.correct_answer: Variable cost, capacity, and contribution under the new method.
questions.rationale: Delivery changes can affect costs and capacity even if customer price is unchanged.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Tendaji Tutorial 04-025 is considering a tailoring pickup service for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a prototype exposed confusion at one step; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. How handle uncertain cost estimates?
options: Label them, document their basis, and test those capable of changing the decision.
Present the most favorable estimate as fact.
Remove uncertain costs.
Use false precision.
questions.correct_answer: Label them, document their basis, and test those capable of changing the decision.
questions.rationale: Transparent estimates and ranges are more useful than unsupported precision or omission.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Tendaji Tutorial 04-025 is considering a tailoring pickup service for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a prototype exposed confusion at one step; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. What does cash runway estimate?
options: Certain customer purchases next year.
Lifetime accounting profit.
Units needed to cover variable costs only.
How long available cash may cover expected net outflows under stated assumptions.
questions.correct_answer: How long available cash may cover expected net outflows under stated assumptions.
questions.rationale: Runway is conditional and changes with spending, receipts, timing, and financing.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Tendaji Tutorial 04-025 is considering a tailoring pickup service for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a prototype exposed confusion at one step; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. Why distinguish profit from cash flow?
options: Cash flow counts customer compliments.
Profit excludes every cash-paid cost.
Revenue recognition and expenses may occur at different times from cash receipts and payments.
They are always equal in small firms.
questions.correct_answer: Revenue recognition and expenses may occur at different times from cash receipts and payments.
questions.rationale: Timing, credit, inventory, and accounting items can separate reported profit from available cash.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Tendaji Tutorial 04-025 is considering a tailoring pickup service for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a prototype exposed confusion at one step; one constraint is that customers need clear terms before a deposit. A forecast relies on high repeat purchases. What is best practice?
options: Ignore it because it concerns future customers.
Model alternative repeat rates and identify evidence needed to support each.
Use only the high case for a funding request.
Treat a spreadsheet assumption as fact.
questions.correct_answer: Model alternative repeat rates and identify evidence needed to support each.
questions.rationale: Scenarios reveal sensitivity to uncertain drivers and the evidence needed for decisions.

assessments.concept_explanation: Unit economics relate revenue and costs to a defined transaction or customer unit and test contribution toward fixed obligations.

assessments.why_it_matters: A venture can have orders yet lose money or lack cash; unit and timing analysis make decisions more grounded.
assessments.how_it_works: Define a unit and period, identify costs, calculate contribution, and compare it with overhead. Model timing and uncertain inputs separately.
assessments.worked_examples: For Tendaji Tutorial 04-025, include actual packaging, delivery, and payment costs for a tailoring pickup service; label estimates and test customers need clear terms before a deposit before inferring margin.
assessments.common_mistakes: Revenue is not profit; positive contribution does not prove overhead is covered; an invoice is not necessarily collected cash.
assessments.practical_application: Build a per-unit table, label observed and estimated inputs, reconcile actual orders, and verify a key assumption from a prototype exposed confusion at one step.
assessments.decisions_and_tradeoffs: Detailed tracking takes time; prioritize variables that could change the decision and use transparent ranges for uncertainty.
assessments.related_concepts: Unit economics link pricing, operations, acquisition, funding, and runway; break-even estimates rely on consistent assumptions, not certainty.

Reason from the stated evidence, separate facts from assumptions, and account for this scenario's constraint: local permit requirements remain unverified.
learning_objectives: Separate variable costs, fixed costs, contribution, profit, and cash.
Apply break-even reasoning to stated assumptions.
Use scenarios to reveal sensitivity to uncertain economic inputs.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Soko Tutorial 04-032 is considering a low-waste lunch plan for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a review found delays around one dependency; one constraint is that local permit requirements remain unverified. How is contribution per sale calculated?
options: Revenue minus every historical startup expense.
Fixed costs divided by competitors.
Cash balance plus unpaid invoices.
Revenue per sale minus variable costs attributable to that sale.
questions.correct_answer: Revenue per sale minus variable costs attributable to that sale.
questions.rationale: Contribution is available toward fixed costs; it is not identical to profit or cash.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Soko Tutorial 04-032 is considering a low-waste lunch plan for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a review found delays around one dependency; one constraint is that local permit requirements remain unverified. Orders have positive contribution but overhead is uncovered. What follows?
options: Overhead can be ignored.
An unpaid invoice counts as received cash.
More contribution volume, improved unit economics, or lower fixed costs may be needed for break-even.
The business is already profitable.
questions.correct_answer: More contribution volume, improved unit economics, or lower fixed costs may be needed for break-even.
questions.rationale: Per-unit contribution alone does not establish that fixed obligations are covered.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Soko Tutorial 04-032 is considering a low-waste lunch plan for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a review found delays around one dependency; one constraint is that local permit requirements remain unverified. Which is a variable cost per delivery?
options: A long-term strategic objective.
Packaging and courier charges incurred for each fulfilled order.
A monthly lease unchanged by order volume.
A registration fee already paid once.
questions.correct_answer: Packaging and courier charges incurred for each fulfilled order.
questions.rationale: A variable cost changes with transactions or units; the other examples do not in this scenario.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Soko Tutorial 04-032 is considering a low-waste lunch plan for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a review found delays around one dependency; one constraint is that local permit requirements remain unverified. Why account for founder labor in unit economics?
options: It reveals dependence on unpaid work that may later need to be paid or replaced.
It makes unpaid time current cash expenditure.
It eliminates fixed costs.
It turns labor into sales revenue.
questions.correct_answer: It reveals dependence on unpaid work that may later need to be paid or replaced.
questions.rationale: Valuing owner labor exposes economic dependence without misclassifying current cash flow.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Soko Tutorial 04-032 is considering a low-waste lunch plan for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a review found delays around one dependency; one constraint is that local permit requirements remain unverified. Given fixed costs and positive unit contribution, how estimate break-even quantity?
options: Divide revenue by employee count.
Divide variable cost by fixed costs.
Multiply cash balance by price.
Divide fixed costs by contribution per unit using consistent assumptions.
questions.correct_answer: Divide fixed costs by contribution per unit using consistent assumptions.
questions.rationale: The ratio estimates units needed for contribution to cover fixed costs under the model.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Soko Tutorial 04-032 is considering a low-waste lunch plan for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a review found delays around one dependency; one constraint is that local permit requirements remain unverified. The delivery method changes. What should be recalculated?
options: Only social reactions to the announcement.
Treat each extra delivery as pure margin.
Variable cost, capacity, and contribution under the new method.
Nothing because price stayed the same.
questions.correct_answer: Variable cost, capacity, and contribution under the new method.
questions.rationale: Delivery changes can affect costs and capacity even if customer price is unchanged.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Soko Tutorial 04-032 is considering a low-waste lunch plan for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a review found delays around one dependency; one constraint is that local permit requirements remain unverified. How handle uncertain cost estimates?
options: Use false precision.
Label them, document their basis, and test those capable of changing the decision.
Present the most favorable estimate as fact.
Remove uncertain costs.
questions.correct_answer: Label them, document their basis, and test those capable of changing the decision.
questions.rationale: Transparent estimates and ranges are more useful than unsupported precision or omission.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Soko Tutorial 04-032 is considering a low-waste lunch plan for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a review found delays around one dependency; one constraint is that local permit requirements remain unverified. What does cash runway estimate?
options: How long available cash may cover expected net outflows under stated assumptions.
Certain customer purchases next year.
Lifetime accounting profit.
Units needed to cover variable costs only.
questions.correct_answer: How long available cash may cover expected net outflows under stated assumptions.
questions.rationale: Runway is conditional and changes with spending, receipts, timing, and financing.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Soko Tutorial 04-032 is considering a low-waste lunch plan for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a review found delays around one dependency; one constraint is that local permit requirements remain unverified. Why distinguish profit from cash flow?
options: They are always equal in small firms.
Cash flow counts customer compliments.
Profit excludes every cash-paid cost.
Revenue recognition and expenses may occur at different times from cash receipts and payments.
questions.correct_answer: Revenue recognition and expenses may occur at different times from cash receipts and payments.
questions.rationale: Timing, credit, inventory, and accounting items can separate reported profit from available cash.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Soko Tutorial 04-032 is considering a low-waste lunch plan for small offices managing supplies. Its current evidence is that a review found delays around one dependency; one constraint is that local permit requirements remain unverified. A forecast relies on high repeat purchases. What is best practice?
options: Treat a spreadsheet assumption as fact.
Ignore it because it concerns future customers.
Model alternative repeat rates and identify evidence needed to support each.
Use only the high case for a funding request.
questions.correct_answer: Model alternative repeat rates and identify evidence needed to support each.
questions.rationale: Scenarios reveal sensitivity to uncertain drivers and the evidence needed for decisions.

assessments.concept_explanation: Unit economics relate revenue and costs to a defined transaction or customer unit and test contribution toward fixed obligations.
assessments.terminology_and_components: Variable costs change with units; fixed costs do not vary directly within a relevant range; contribution is revenue less associated variable costs.
assessments.why_it_matters: A venture can have orders yet lose money or lack cash; unit and timing analysis make decisions more grounded.
assessments.how_it_works: Define a unit and period, identify costs, calculate contribution, and compare it with overhead. Model timing and uncertain inputs separately.
assessments.worked_examples: For Soko Tutorial 04-032, include actual packaging, delivery, and payment costs for a low-waste lunch plan; label estimates and test local permit requirements remain unverified before inferring margin.
assessments.common_mistakes: Revenue is not profit; positive contribution does not prove overhead is covered; an invoice is not necessarily collected cash.
assessments.practical_application: Build a per-unit table, label observed and estimated inputs, reconcile actual orders, and verify a key assumption from a review found delays around one dependency.
assessments.decisions_and_tradeoffs: Detailed tracking takes time; prioritize variables that could change the decision and use transparent ranges for uncertainty.
assessments.related_concepts: Unit economics link pricing, operations, acquisition, funding, and runway; break-even estimates rely on consistent assumptions, not certainty.

assessments.title: Entrepreneurship: Pricing and value exchange — Lengo Tutorial 05-033
assessments.description: Apply pricing and value exchange to an illustrative venture considering an event-supplies rental for repair customers with limited time. Reason from the stated evidence, separate facts from assumptions, and account for this scenario's constraint: a partner's response time is uncertain.
learning_objectives: Explain how value, alternatives, and delivery costs inform price.
Distinguish stated willingness from observed purchase behavior.
Assess pricing experiments for margin, clarity, and fairness.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Lengo Tutorial 05-033 is considering an event-supplies rental for repair customers with limited time. Its current evidence is that two groups used different workarounds for the same outcome; one constraint is that a partner's response time is uncertain. What is a sound starting point for price?
options: Choose only what seems affordable to the founder.
Price below cost and assume volume fixes the gap.
Test a clear price while examining customer value, alternatives, and delivery cost.
Copy a competitor without comparing offers.
questions.correct_answer: Test a clear price while examining customer value, alternatives, and delivery cost.
questions.rationale: Pricing combines value, alternatives, costs, and strategy; no shortcut establishes a universal right price.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Lengo Tutorial 05-033 is considering an event-supplies rental for repair customers with limited time. Its current evidence is that two groups used different workarounds for the same outcome; one constraint is that a partner's response time is uncertain. A willingness-to-pay interview establishes what?
options: That cost and capacity can be ignored.
A stated response in that conversation, to compare with observed choices where possible.
A guaranteed future purchase.
The exact price all customers accept.
questions.correct_answer: A stated response in that conversation, to compare with observed choices where possible.
questions.rationale: Stated willingness is evidence, not a completed purchase or universal market price.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Lengo Tutorial 05-033 is considering an event-supplies rental for repair customers with limited time. Its current evidence is that two groups used different workarounds for the same outcome; one constraint is that a partner's response time is uncertain. Why compare prices using the same offer and comparable customers?
options: It helps isolate price response from changes in features, audience, or messaging.
It ensures the highest price wins.
It makes context irrelevant.
It removes the need to define conversion.
questions.correct_answer: It helps isolate price response from changes in features, audience, or messaging.
questions.rationale: A controlled comparison clarifies interpretation, though a test may still have limits.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Lengo Tutorial 05-033 is considering an event-supplies rental for repair customers with limited time. Its current evidence is that two groups used different workarounds for the same outcome; one constraint is that a partner's response time is uncertain. A discount increases orders but reduces contribution. What should be examined?
options: Order count alone.
Gross revenue without fulfillment costs.
Popularity among people who did not order.
Whether incremental contribution and learning justify lower margin and capacity demands.
questions.correct_answer: Whether incremental contribution and learning justify lower margin and capacity demands.
questions.rationale: Volume is not the only outcome; consider contribution, customer fit, capacity, and the promotion's purpose.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Lengo Tutorial 05-033 is considering an event-supplies rental for repair customers with limited time. Its current evidence is that two groups used different workarounds for the same outcome; one constraint is that a partner's response time is uncertain. What is price anchoring?
options: A measure of variable cost.
A reason to invent a former price.
A reference price can influence perception and should be truthful and relevant.
A guarantee of acceptance at any price.
questions.correct_answer: A reference price can influence perception and should be truthful and relevant.
questions.rationale: Anchors affect comparisons, but fabricated references are misleading and can erode trust.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Lengo Tutorial 05-033 is considering an event-supplies rental for repair customers with limited time. Its current evidence is that two groups used different workarounds for the same outcome; one constraint is that a partner's response time is uncertain. How make tiers easier for customers to assess?
options: Make an optional tier appear mandatory.
Define material differences in scope or service and disclose each tier's limits.
Use confusing names for identical terms.
Hide the least expensive tier until checkout.
questions.correct_answer: Define material differences in scope or service and disclose each tier's limits.
questions.rationale: Clear differences support informed choice and avoid deceptive choice design.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Lengo Tutorial 05-033 is considering an event-supplies rental for repair customers with limited time. Its current evidence is that two groups used different workarounds for the same outcome; one constraint is that a partner's response time is uncertain. When is a time-limited promotion defensible?
options: When the genuine end condition and eligibility are accurately stated.
When a deadline resets to pressure buyers.
When the regular price was never charged.
When fees appear only after commitment.
questions.correct_answer: When the genuine end condition and eligibility are accurately stated.
questions.rationale: Real limits and transparent terms are fairer than artificial urgency or hidden charges.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Lengo Tutorial 05-033 is considering an event-supplies rental for repair customers with limited time. Its current evidence is that two groups used different workarounds for the same outcome; one constraint is that a partner's response time is uncertain. Why consider acquisition cost alongside price?
options: It proves all customers return.
It replaces fulfillment-cost tracking.
Referral acquisition is always costless.
Acquisition spending reduces what remains for delivery, overhead, and investment.
questions.correct_answer: Acquisition spending reduces what remains for delivery, overhead, and investment.
questions.rationale: Acquisition cost is one economic input to compare with contribution and retention evidence.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Lengo Tutorial 05-033 is considering an event-supplies rental for repair customers with limited time. Its current evidence is that two groups used different workarounds for the same outcome; one constraint is that a partner's response time is uncertain. Demand exceeds service capacity at the current price. What is responsible?
options: Reduce quality without notice.
Promise a date the team cannot support.
Manage availability or price transparently while protecting service quality.
Accept unlimited orders and hide delays.
questions.correct_answer: Manage availability or price transparently while protecting service quality.
questions.rationale: Price and capacity interact; do not sell commitments the venture cannot reasonably meet.

questions.prompt: Scenario: Lengo Tutorial 05-033 is considering an event-supplies rental for repair customers with limited time. Its current evidence is that two groups used different workarounds for the same outcome; one constraint is that a partner's response time is uncertain. What makes a pricing experiment interpretable?
options: Choosing the favored result after seeing data.
A defined audience, consistent offer, clear price, and preselected behavior measure.
Changing price, product, and audience together.
Counting visits as purchases without stating the difference.
questions.correct_answer: A defined audience, consistent offer, clear price, and preselected behavior measure.
questions.rationale: A clear design supports interpretation while acknowledging that results may not generalize.

assessments.concept_explanation: Pricing reflects value exchanged, alternatives, delivery costs, and objectives; a stated response neither guarantees purchase nor sets a universal price.
assessments.terminology_and_components: Willingness to pay may be stated or observed; contribution accounts for variable cost; an anchor influences comparison; promotion terms must be truthful.
assessments.why_it_matters: Price affects access, perceived value, demand, capacity, and service resources. Hidden fees and careless discounts can harm trust.
assessments.how_it_works: Define offer and audience, investigate alternatives and costs, then test clear prices and track intended behavior and contribution.
assessments.worked_examples: For Lengo Tutorial 05-033, show comparable repair customers with limited time prospects the same an event-supplies rental scope at a clear test price; distinguish actions from reactions and account for a partner's response time is uncertain.
assessments.common_mistakes: Copying a competitor, treating survey answers as sales, changing offer details during a test, or inventing a former price weakens evidence.
assessments.practical_application: State scope, price, exclusions, and payment timing plainly; compare response to unit cost and capacity.
assessments.decisions_and_tradeoffs: A lower price may improve access but reduce contribution; a higher price can support service while excluding some customers. Test openly.
assessments.related_concepts: Pricing depends on discovery, positioning, unit economics, channel costs, and operations; promotions also involve ethical communication.
